title: Misc Office Ops and Runtime Quirks
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This page is a deliberately miscellaneous collection of operational notes, small runbook fragments, and a handful of office logistics items that surfaced during on-call rotations and weekly runtime syncs. It is not a canonical architecture doc; treat items here as context-rich noise that may be useful when triaging odd runtime behaviours or planning small infrastructural housekeeping.

Purpose:
- Capture small, non-actionable observations about serving-runtime quirks.
- Keep a short checklist for low-cost office operations (vending, supplies) so on-call folks can avoid interruptions.
- Surface minor suggestions that don't yet warrant a full ADR or Confluence page.

Quick summary of notable runtime quirks (engineering context):
1) Occasional small-object GC pauses seen when background maintenance jobs overlap with burst traffic windows. Hypothesis: Python-based admin tasks touching model caches cause incremental memory pressure and CPU spikes on control-plane nodes.
2) Batching spikes when request size distribution shifts (more short queries than expected) leading to suboptimal packing. Temporary mitigation: reduce max-wait-ms in the inference router for affected prefix.
3) KV cache fragmentation after rolling restarts in mixed-quantization pools; increase measured tail latency by ~10–15ms for cold prefix workloads.

Actionable suggestions (short):
- For short-term GC pauses: schedule heavy control-plane jobs (snapshot, compliance exports) outside peak hours (US morning).
- For batching variance: add histogram metrics for request token-length by route to auto-detect distribution shifts.
- For KV fragmentation: include a lightweight post-rolling-check that validates KV consistency and warms the top N prefixes.

Office ops (non-technical but useful for continuity):
- Vending machine: restock request process: slack #facilities with photo, item list, and preferred vendor. Typical turnaround ~3 business days.
- Printer toner: shared_drives/engineering/_temp_uploads/toner-orders is the interim order sheet (legacy).

Runbook fragment: diagnosing a small spike in tail latency (<= 1 hour incident)
1) Check the Console SLO dashboard for the route and time range, confirm affected percentiles (p50/p90/p99).
2) Query recent deploys and rolling restarts: grep deploy logs for the service tag; correlate to control-plane maintenance jobs.
3) Inspect batching metrics: batching_queue_time_ms, batch_fill_ratio, and avg_tokens_per_request. If batch_fill_ratio < 0.6 and batch_size smaller than expected, consider temporarily lowering max-wait-ms on router.
4) Check KV cache hit rate and last_warm_timestamp for model variants. If hit rate < 85% and last warm < 2 hours, trigger a targeted warm-up (script: scripts/warm_prefixes.sh --top 50).
5) If CPU steal or I/O wait is high on nodes, check noisy-neighbor signals and recent dedicated capacity autoscaling events.

Small configuration table (example thresholds used by on-call)
- SLO target (route default): 95% requests <= 120ms, p99 <= 500ms
- Alert thresholds: p95 > 200ms for 5m OR p99 > 600ms for 1m
- Batching: default max-wait-ms = 12, max-batch-tokens = 4096
- KV cache warm threshold: < 85% hit triggers warm-up

Checklist for adding trivial housekeeping items to this page:
1) Add item with a short title and one-paragraph rationale.
2) If the item is clearly actionable in < 1 hour, move to eng-sre action list and assign.
3) If the item is long-form, draft an ADR and link from here.

Ownership and escalation:
- Maintainer: eng-serving-runtime on-call rotation (primary contact via PagerDuty).
- Triage owner for office ops items: facilities@redwood-inference (use internal alias).
- For anything tagged security or legal, escalate to security-and-compliance and stop; do not document sensitive details here.

Related artifacts and links:
- Deploy checklist: confluence/eng-serving-runtime/deploy-checklist
- Incident playbook: confluence/eng-sre/incident-response
- Warm-up script (repo): github/redwood/tools/warm-prefixes (note: small helper script, may be moved)

Notes and miscellaneous noise (explicitly informal):
- Coffee machine cycles correlate poorly with sprint deadlines but this is anecdotal.
- We keep a small spare HDMI->DP dongle in the engineering kitchenette labeled "borrow me." Return within 48 hours.
- If you find a half-eaten sandwich near the NUC rack, please notify facilities and remove before it attracts pests.
